metadata.title: Examining adults’ web navigation patterns in multi-layered hypertext environments

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses OECD PIAAC 2012 log files for the Problem Solving in Technology-Rich Environments (PSTRE) domain, but the analysis is restricted to two specific PSTRE tasks (book purchase and reliable site) and only to participants from the United States and the United Kingdom who worked on both tasks. The authors report extracting clickstream variables from task log files and then applying latent class analysis (LCA) and full-path sequence analysis to identify navigation pattern groups; they do not describe the use of PIAAC sampling weights or replicate weights in the estimation of these models. Because the paper does not mention any weight variables (e.g., TOTWGT or W_FSTUWT) or complex survey design adjustments, weighting is treated as not applied/undocumented for the reported pattern identification and correctness comparisons. Analysts using the same PIAAC log data should verify whether OECD-provided weights are available for these log-based subsamples and, if population-representative inference is desired, apply the appropriate PIAAC weights when estimating group distributions and task correctness differences.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This study does not model cognitive achievement scores with PIAAC Plausible Values; instead, it analyzes clickstream navigation behavior and uses task correctness (dichotomously scored 0/1) as the effectiveness outcome. Because the dependent variables are task correctness and navigation-pattern group membership derived from log-based behavioral indicators, PV handling is not applicable. The paper also does not report a missing-data strategy for the log-derived variables used in LCA/sequence analysis, so missing-data handling is not reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Source data are PIAAC 2012 PSTRE log files. The authors extracted only the two PSTRE tasks used in the analysis: the book purchase task and the reliable site task. They further restricted the dataset to participants from the United States and the United Kingdom who worked on both tasks (US N=659; UK N=1182), then removed participants who pressed the next button before clicking on any links on a SERP (to ensure navigation occurred). The final analytic sample is N=1408 (494 US; 914 UK). For analysis, clickstream data were divided into two subsets per country (one per task), and LCA was run separately for each task and country using observed variables defined as the amounts of visits to each web page.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using OECD PIAAC 2012 PSTRE log the study analyzed adults’ clickstream navigation patterns in two simulated multi-layered hypertext web-search tasks: the book purchase task and the reliable site task. The analytic sample comprised 494 adults from the United States and 914 adults from the United Kingdom, after excluding participants who advanced without clicking any SERP links. The authors identified latent navigation pattern groups via latent class analysis on page-visit counts and then characterized typical behavior using full-path sequence analysis; they report task correctness differences across pattern groups using Pearson chi-square tests and post-hoc pairwise comparisons. For the book purchase task, the Satisficing pattern group achieved the highest correctness (US: 96.05%; UK: 93.55%), while for the reliable site task the Sampling pattern group was highest (US: 92.45%; UK: 92.90%). The study’s limitations include restricted task environments (restricted information space and two tasks only) and no reported use of PIAAC sampling/replicate weights for these log-based pattern and correctness comparisons. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an empirical process-data study focused on identifying navigation pattern groups (via LCA and sequence analysis) and comparing their task correctness; it does not train or evaluate machine-learning predictive models. Consequently, the schema’s ML technique fields are empty and no PV-based achievement modeling is performed. The paper also does not report a missing-data handling procedure for the log-derived variables used in LCA/sequence analysis, which is why missing_data_handling is set to not_reported.
